full_judgment: 2. The relevant facts are that the complainant Shashi Mohan Das filed a complaint case in the Court of Senior Special Judge, Sunamganj alleging that he and his brother Hari Mohan were owners of the land in plot No. 1914 appertaining to Khatian No. 70. But the accused Chitta Ranjan Sinha created a forged deed bearing No. 8258 dated 18-10-1960 in which his father was shown purchaser of the property and the complaint's father was shown as a seller. On the basis of this document the accused applied to the Revenue Officer for mutation who instructed opposite party No. 2 Haripad Roy, Tahsilder, to submit a report and he submitted a false report stating that petitioner's father Shyam Lal Das was alive and the accused No.3 Ershad Ali, a process server, gave a false report that the process was duly served. In this way, accused No. 1 in collusion with the accused Nos. 2 and 3 (Public Servant) committed an offence under sections 467/471/109 of the Penal Code and also under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. Accordingly, mutation was duly made in the name of father of accused No. 1 on the basis of the forged deed in the mutation case on 409/96-97. Against the mutation order, the complainant filed an appeal being Appeal No. 6 of 1997 before the Additional Deputy. Commissioner (Revenue), Sunamganj, who ultimately cancelled the aforesaid mutation order. Thereafter the accused No. 1 instituted Title Suit No. 3 of 1997 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sulla on 29-5-97. After receiving the aforesaid complaint, it was registered as Special Case No. 4 of 1997 and the Bureau of Anti-Corruption conducted enquiry on the direction of the Court and found the allegation true and submitted a report to the Senior Special Judge, Sunamganj. Thereafter, cognisance was taken under sections 419/420/467/468/471/109 of the Penal Code and also under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 by his order dated 17-10-99. On 7-5-2000 the accused-petitioner filed an application under section 241-A of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the Senior Special Judge, Sunamganj to discharge him on the grounds that the allegations leveled against him were false and that the complainant not being the ADC (Revenue), the criminal prosecution. was not maintainable as it was barred under section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. But the learned Senior Special Judge rejected the petition and framed the charges against all the accused-persons under sections 467/471/109 of the Penal Code along with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947.
